scenes: narrator
What happens to a date palm when it stops giving fruit?
narrator
For Abu Salim, it was the start of a very hard season.
narrator
He had to cut his old palms down. But the heavy trunks just lay there.
narrator
Burning them meant smoke. Leaving them meant waste.
narrator
Then ARIBS came to his farm, collected every trunk, and lifted the burden off his shoulders.
narrator
At our factory in Barka, those old palm trunks become natural palm peat.
narrator
Packed in sealed two-hundred-litre bags, or supplied loose, by the kilo or the ton.
narrator
And it comes back home, to farms across Oman, even to Abu Salim's.
narrator
Mixed into the soil, palm peat holds water longer, so every drop goes further.
narrator
Today, his farm is full of life again.
narrator
No burning. No waste. Just better soil, made in Oman.
narrator
ARIBS. Turning old palms into a greener Oman.
